# Wetland -- standalone C++ solver generated by OpenHydroQual

Every model equation is hard-coded (no expression interpreter). The folder is
self-contained: no Qt, no Armadillo, no OpenHydroQual install needed.

## Files
- `Wetland.h` -- the generated model class (10 state variables, 13 links, 1 constituent(s))
- `runtime/` -- header-only solver runtime (mass balance, sparse/dense Newton, time series)
- `Wetland_api.h/.cpp` -- C ABI wrapper (callable from C, Python ctypes, Fortran, ...)
- `example.cpp` -- minimal client
- `CMakeLists.txt`

## Build
```
# Linux / macOS
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build

# Windows (Visual Studio 2022)
cmake -S . -B build -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A x64
cmake --build build --config Release
```

## Use
Link `Wetland` and include `Wetland_api.h`:
```c
Wetland_handle* h = Wetland_create();
Wetland_initialize(h);
Wetland_run_to(h, Wetland_simulation_end());
double v = Wetland_state(h, 0);   /* see Wetland_state_name(0) */
Wetland_destroy(h);
```
Or use the C++ class directly: `#include "Wetland.h"` -> `initialize()`, `step()`, `stepTo(t)`, `runTo(t)`, `time()`, `state(i)`.

## Model time window
`tstart = 40178.8`, `tend = 40542.8`, `dt0 = 0.01`
